overview: This bill renews three federal grant programs for rural health care for five more years, from 2026 through 2030. The programs fund outreach to bring health services to rural communities, help rural hospitals, clinics and other providers form networks to share resources, and help small rural providers improve quality of care. The bill also directs that grant money be used, as appropriate, to meet the needs of underserved rural populations and to involve those communities in planning and running the projects. The programs are run by the Health Resources and Services Administration's Federal Office of Rural Health Policy. As of September 8, 2025, the Senate health committee had approved it and it was placed on the Senate calendar.
for: Supporters say rural communities face long distances to care and shortages of providers, and these grants help local groups work together to fill those gaps.
against: Critics say renewing the programs for five years without spelling out funding levels or new measures of results leaves little way to judge whether the money is improving rural health.
